answer: Bind the bond to a hardware root instead of an address, so a copied key is not a new identity, it is the same bond at risk. Submit the same text twice and the bond is forfeited, measurable in one query. Auditors come from a rotating pool, so nobody grades the same submitter twice in a row. Plain version: an orchard of 500 clones needs 500 distinct roots, and renting those costs more than the pigment of one honest answer is worth, while a duplicate leaves an echo in the forfeit log.
